misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component - EVM instructions are internal to the execution environment, not external entities
Internal component - Calling function within the same system boundary
Ambiguous - Could be internal if it's the node's own RPC service; treating as internal when client is querying its own node

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user submitting contract creation transactions via network. No authentication required for transaction submission. All transaction data must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled as adversarial entity attempting DoS attacks. Default untrusted - represents worst-case threat model.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying RPC methods. Network peer with no authentication requirement specified. Input must be validated per JSON-RPC spec.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Method Caller
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any external entity making JSON-RPC calls. No authentication implied. All method parameters must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web Browser User
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User navigating to web pages. User actions trigger navigation to potentially malicious sites. Security context checks required before provider injection.

trusted_external_entities.name: Website/DApp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External website requesting Ethereum provider access. Even HTTPS sites can be malicious. Secure context validation required before granting access.

trusted_external_entities.name: Third-Party Advertisement
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Third-party iframe explicitly described as potentially malicious. Must be blocked from provider access by default.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Developer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Developer running local development server. Access is gated behind explicit dev mode toggle that user must enable. Still semi-trusted as localhost can be compromised.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required including initcode size check (max 49152 bytes), signature verification, and gas validation.
EIP-3860 size limits mitigate DoS via jumpdest analysis. Attacker must pay ~80M additional gas for attack, making it economically infeasible.
rpc.discover method should only return method specifications. No sensitive data exposed. Rate limiting may be needed to prevent resource exhaustion.
Method namespace checking required. Reserved 'rpc.' prefix methods should be handled specially. Input validation on all parameters.
Secure context check (isSecureContext) and trustworthy origin verification required before provider injection. HTTP non-localhost must be blocked.

coverage_gaps.reason: No direct edge from EXT-WEBSITE in the subgraph; security boundary is mediated through user navigation
